title: Sicilia Holds Just Below the National Average as Prices Ease for a Second Day
dek: Self-service Benzina and Gasolio in Sicilia both edged down again on August 5th, keeping the island a hair cheaper than Italy as a whole.
body: Self-service drivers in Sicilia paid €2.011 for Benzina and €2.151 for Gasolio on August 5th, both fractionally above the national self-service averages of €2.010 and €2.125. Petrol on the island is now essentially tied with the rest of the country, while diesel runs about two and a half cents higher than the national figure — a gap that has narrowed steadily over the past week.

The trend has been gently downward: Sicilia's self-service Benzina slipped from €2.012 on August 4th to €2.011 on the 5th, and Gasolio fell from €2.155 to €2.151 over the same span, extending a soft two-day pullback after prices had crept up through late July. Behind those figures, the regional station network stayed steady: 1,995 stations are registered across Sicilia, with 1,783 reporting prices on the 5th, a solid 89% reporting rate that shows the island's network is still being tracked closely day to day.
